items.stem: What is the gross cropped area ?

options.label: A
options.text: Area sown more than once in an agricultural year plus net sown area

options.label: B
options.text: Area sown more than once in an agricultural year minus net sown area

options.label: C
options.text: Area sown with crops but is counted only once.

options.label: D
options.text: Double of the area sown more than once in an agricultural year

items.answer: Gross cropped area counts every sowing on a field in one agricultural year. It is therefore the area sown more than once in an agricultural year added to the net sown area, so the same field counted twice if two crops are raised on it. Hence the gross cropped area is the area sown more than once in an agricultural year plus the net sown area.

items.stem: Assertion - Arid soil is unsuitable for cultivation. Reason : Arid soil is generally sandy in texture and saline in nature. It restricts the filtration of water.
items.assertion: Arid soil is unsuitable for cultivation.
items.reason: Arid soil is generally sandy in texture and saline in nature. It restricts the filtration of water.

options.label: A
options.text: Both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.

options.label: B
options.text: Both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion is true but reason is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Both assertion and reason are false.

items.answer: Arid soil is sandy, saline and poor in humus and moisture, so in its natural state it does not support cultivation - the assertion is true. The reason, however, is wrong on the physics: a sandy arid soil lets water percolate away quickly rather than restricting its filtration, which is precisely why it cannot hold moisture for crops. So the assertion is true but the reason is false.

items.stem: What is the net sown area ?

options.label: A
options.text: Area sown more than once in an agricultural year plus net sown area

options.label: B
options.text: Area sown more than once in an agricultural year minus net sown area

options.label: C
options.text: Area sown with crops but is counted only once.

options.label: D
options.text: Double of the area sown more than once in an agricultural year

items.answer: Net sown area is the physical area on which crops are actually raised in an agricultural year, each field being counted once however many times it is cropped. Hence it is the area sown with crops but counted only once.
items.ocr: Printed key letter is (c); the book then restates it as the garbled, truncated line 'Net area sown more than once in an agricultural', which does not reproduce option (c)'s printed text. Letter (c) is kept because it is both the printed key and the correct definition.

items.stem: What is the percentage of the culturable waste land in India?
items.answer: Of India's reporting area, culturable waste land - land left uncultivated for more than five agricultural years - accounts for 4.41 per cent. Hence the answer is 4.41%.

items.stem: Fallow land is a kind of agricultural land. It is ________ fertile.
items.answer: Fallow land is cultivable land that is deliberately left uncropped for a season or a few years so that it can recover its lost nutrients. While it is resting it yields nothing and is the poorer of the agricultural categories in fertility at that moment. Hence fallow land is less fertile.

items.stem:
Match the following columns :
Column-I (Type of Soil)Column-II (Crops Grown)
A. Arid soil1. Cotton and groundnut
B. Black soil2. Jowar and Bajra
C. Laterite soil3. Tea and coffee
D. Mountain/Forest soil4. Cashew and spices
items.answer: Arid soil of the dry north-west supports hardy millets, jowar and bajra, so A-2. Black regur soil of the Deccan is the classic cotton and groundnut soil, so B-1. Laterite soil of the humid hills of Kerala and Karnataka grows cashew and spices, so C-4. Mountain and forest soil of the hill slopes is where tea and coffee plantations are raised, so D-3. The matching is A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3.

items.stem:
Arrange the following types of soil found as the major soil types in India from north to south-
1. Forest and mountainous soil.
2. Black soil.
3. Alluvial soil.
4. Red and Yellow soil.
items.answer: Moving down the country from the Himalaya, the first belt is forest and mountainous soil on the northern ranges, then the alluvial soil of the northern plains, then the black soil of the Deccan lava region, and finally the red and yellow soil of the southern peninsular crystalline uplands. The order from north to south is therefore 1, 3, 2, 4.

items.stem: What name is given to the land which is left free for 1 to 5 years uncultivated?
items.answer: Land that is fit for cultivation but is left unsown for a spell of about one to five years is grouped with culturable wasteland in the land-use record, since the land can be brought back under the plough. Hence it is called culturable wasteland.

items.stem:
Identify the process-
• Is a gradual process.
• It is the displacement of the upper layer of soil.
• Is a natural process.
• Caused by the dynamic activity of water, ice, snow, air, plants, animals and humans.
items.answer: The clues describe the slow removal of the topmost layer of soil by running water, wind, ice and by human and animal activity. That denudation of the upper soil cover is soil erosion.

items.stem: Assertion - Controlling on mining activities doesn't control land degradation. Reason : In states like Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, deforestation has occurred due to overgrazing, not minings
items.assertion: Controlling on mining activities doesn't control land degradation.
items.reason: In states like Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, deforestation has occurred due to overgrazing, not minings

options.label: A
options.text: Both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.

options.label: B
options.text: Both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion is true but reason is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Both assertion and reason are false.

items.answer: Mining is one of the principal human causes of land degradation - abandoned pits and the deep scars of mining in Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha leave land unusable - so regulating mining does help check degradation and the assertion is false. The reason is false too: in Gujarat, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh overgrazing is indeed a major cause of degradation, but mining is also at work there, so the flat denial of mining is wrong. Both assertion and reason are false.

items.stem: Which of the following is not a physical factor to determine land use?
items.answer: Climate, soil type and topography are all natural attributes of a place and so are physical determinants of how land is used. Population density is a human factor, not a physical one. Hence population density is not a physical factor.

items.stem: The total geographical area of India is ____.
items.answer: India covers about 3.28 million square kilometres of land, of which land-use records are available for only about 93 per cent. Hence the total geographical area is 3.28 million square kilometre.

items.stem:
Arrange the following in the correct sequence (land degradation by percentage:
1. Forest degraded area
2. Water eroded area
3. Wind eroded area
4. Saline and alkaline deposits
items.answer: Taking the shares of degraded land in descending order, water erosion accounts for the largest part, followed by degraded forest area, then wind-eroded area, and the smallest share is the saline and alkaline deposits. The sequence is therefore 2, 1, 3, 4.

items.stem: What is the percentage of net sown area out of the total reporting area in India?
items.answer: The net sown area of India works out to about 54 per cent of the total reporting area, though it varies sharply from state to state. Hence the answer is 54 per cent.
items.ocr: Stem and options print at the foot of page 9; the 'Ans :' line and key print at the head of page 10.

items.stem: The pattern of net sown area varies greatly from one state to another. It is over ___ percent of the total area in Punjab and Haryana.
items.answer: Punjab and Haryana are intensively farmed plains states, and in both of them the net sown area exceeds 80 per cent of the total area, against a national figure of about 54 per cent. Hence the answer is 80.

items.stem:
'Study the picture and answer the question that follows:
Which of the following best signifies the above image?
items.answer: The picture shows bacteria, a bee and a tree - all of them living organisms. Resources obtained from the biosphere and having life are classified on the basis of origin as biotic resources. Hence the image signifies biotic resources.

items.stem: What is the main reason behind global ecological crises such as global warming and environmental pollution ?

options.label: B
options.text: Accumulation of resources in a few hand

items.answer: Using resources merely for immediate gain, without thought for how much is left or what the waste does, is what has driven global warming, ozone depletion and pollution. The root cause is therefore the indiscriminate exploitation of resources.

items.stem:
Arrange the following layers of soil from top to bottom in a soil profile-
1. Substratum weathered parent rock material.
2. Unweathered parent bed rock.
3. Top soil.
4. Subsoil weathered rocks, sand and slit clay.
items.answer: A soil profile begins at the surface with the top soil, below which lies the subsoil of weathered rock, sand and silty clay, then the substratum of weathered parent rock material, and at the base the unweathered parent bed rock. The order from top to bottom is 3, 4, 1, 2.

options.label: A

options.label: B

options.label: C
options.text: Area sown with crops but is counted only once.

options.label: D
options.text: Double of the area sown more than once in an agricultural year

items.answer: Net sown area is the land actually put under crops in an agricultural year, each field counted once no matter how many crops it carries. Hence it is the area sown with crops but counted only once.
items.ocr: Same wording as question 41. Printed key letter (c) is followed by the garbled, truncated restatement 'Net area sown more than once in an agricultural', which does not reproduce option (c)'s printed text; letter (c) kept.

items.stem: Assertion - Terrace cultivation does not restrict erosion. Reason : Running water cuts through the clayey soils and makes deep channels as gullies. This helps to cultivate crops.
items.assertion: Terrace cultivation does not restrict erosion.
items.reason: Running water cuts through the clayey soils and makes deep channels as gullies. This helps to cultivate crops.

options.label: A
options.text: Both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.

options.label: B
options.text: Both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion is true but reason is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Both assertion and reason are false.

items.answer: Terrace cultivation on steep slopes breaks the length of the slope and slows the run-off, so it does restrict erosion - the assertion is false. Gullies cut by running water through clayey soil ruin the land and turn it into bad land unfit for cultivation, so they certainly do not help crops - the reason is false as well. Both assertion and reason are false.

items.stem: Which among the following is a type of resources classified on the basis of exhaustibility?
items.answer: Classified by exhaustibility, resources fall into those that can be renewed or reproduced by physical, chemical or mechanical processes and those whose stock is finite and takes a geological age to form. That pair is renewable and non-renewable resources. Biotic and abiotic is a classification by origin, national and individual by ownership, and potential and reserves by the stage of development.

items.stem:
Match the following items given in column-I with those in column-II. Choose the correct answer from the codes given below :
Column-IColumn-II
A. Gully erosion1. Develop under tropical and subtropical climate
B. Bad land2. Old Alluvial soil
C. Laterite soil3. Chambal Basin
D. Bhangar4. Land unfit for cultivation
items.answer: Gully erosion is typified by the ravines of the Chambal basin, so A-3. Bad land is land so cut up by ravines that it is unfit for cultivation, so B-4. Laterite soil develops under a tropical and subtropical climate with alternating wet and dry spells, so C-1. Bhangar is the older alluvium of the plains, so D-2. The matching is A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2.

items.stem:
Which of the following is correct for laterite soil ?
(i) It develops under tropical and subtropical climate with alternative wet and dry season.
(ii) There soil are sticky when wet.
items.answer: Laterite soil is indeed the product of a tropical and subtropical climate with alternating wet and dry seasons, in which heavy rain leaches the soil and intense heat bakes it - statement (i) is correct. Stickiness when wet is a property of black cotton soil, not of laterite, so statement (ii) is wrong. Hence only (i) is correct.

items.stem:
Read the information given below and select the correct answer:
Ravi was trying to compare the development of India with her neighbouring countries. He found that Sri Lanka is more developed than India but lacks behind in terms of the size of economy.
What was the indicator used by Ravi to compare the development?
items.answer: Ravi rates Sri Lanka above India on development even though its economy is much smaller, so he cannot be going by income or by the size of national output. A country can rank higher on health, education and living standards while having a smaller economy, and the measure that combines these is the Human Development Index. Hence the indicator used was the Human Development Index.

items.stem:
Study the picture and answer the question that follows:
Which of the following best signifies the above image?
items.answer: The three panels show oil, natural gas and coal. All three are fossil fuels whose stock took millions of years of geological time to form and cannot be replaced once used up. On the basis of exhaustibility they are therefore non-renewable resources.

items.stem:
Identify the resources which the help of following clues -
• They belong to the nation.
• The country has legal powers to acquire even private property for public good.
• example-All the minerals, water resources, forests, wildlife, land within the political boundaries and oceanic area upto 12 nautical miles (22.2 km) from the coast.
Select the appropriate option from the following.
items.answer: Resources that the country owns, that the state may acquire even from private hands for the public good, and that include all minerals, water, forests, wildlife and the land within the political boundary together with the territorial sea up to 12 nautical miles, are national resources.

items.stem:
Match the following columns :
Column-I (Type of Soil)Column-II (States)
A. Laterite soil1. Western Madhya Pradesh
B. Alluvial soil2. Western Rajasthan
C. Black soil3. Karnataka
D. Arid soil4. Uttar Pradesh
items.answer: Laterite soil occurs in the humid uplands of Karnataka, so A-3. Alluvial soil covers the Gangetic plain of Uttar Pradesh, so B-4. Black soil of the Deccan lava country extends into western Madhya Pradesh, so C-1. Arid soil is found in western Rajasthan, so D-2. The matching is A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2.

items.stem:
In the Summit-
• More than 100 heads of states met in Rio de Janeiro in Brazil
• The Summit was convened for addressing urgent problems of environmental protection
• The Rio Convention endorsed the global Forest Principles and adopted Agenda 21
Identify the event :
items.answer: The meeting of more than 100 heads of state at Rio de Janeiro in June 1992, which endorsed the global Forest Principles and adopted Agenda 21, was the first International Earth Summit. Hence the event is the First International Earth Summit.
items.ocr: The book mislabels the third option as '(b)' as well, so the printed labels read (a), (b), (b), (d); the third option is relabelled C here. The third bullet is also printed twice in the book; the duplicate line is dropped.

items.stem:
Identify the event-
• Held in June 1992.
• Covered for addressing urgent problems of environmental protection and socio-economic development at the global level.
• Adopted agenda 21.
• More than 100 heads of states met in this event.
items.answer: June 1992, Agenda 21 and a gathering of more than 100 heads of state on environmental protection and socio-economic development together identify one event - the Earth Summit held at Rio de Janeiro in Brazil in 1992.

items.stem:
Arrange the following soil types found in India as per area covered by them-(From higher to lower)
1. Red soil.
2. Black soil.
3. Arid soil.
4. Alluvial soil.
items.answer: Alluvial soil, spread over the whole northern plain and the deltas, covers the largest area; red soil of the peninsular crystalline uplands comes next; black soil of the Deccan lava region follows; and arid soil, confined to the north-west, covers the smallest area. From higher to lower the order is 4, 1, 2, 3.

items.stem: Assertion - alluvial soil is ideal for the growth of sugarcane, paddy, wheat etc. Reason : It is rich in potash, phosphoric, acid and lime.
items.assertion: alluvial soil is ideal for the growth of sugarcane, paddy, wheat etc.
items.reason: It is rich in potash, phosphoric, acid and lime.

options.label: A
options.text: Both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.

options.label: B
options.text: Both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion is true but reason is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Both assertion and reason are false.

items.answer: Alluvial soil is the most fertile soil of India and carries the intensive cultivation of sugarcane, paddy and wheat across the northern plains, so the assertion is true. It is fertile precisely because it is well supplied with potash, phosphoric acid and lime, the nutrients those crops need, so the reason is true and it explains the assertion. Both are true and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.
